reason: Chat's tool-free final synthesis failed the turn in three ways the live Core logged. A malformed streamed tool call (DeepSeek via OpenRouter: a nameless 2-byte argument fragment) and an upstream refusal frame ('model emitted an undeclared or disallowed function name') surfaced as plain stream errors, skipping the tool_call recovery a well-formed call gets. A response carrying a complete answer plus a tool call (structured, or a trailing DSML frame) was re-asked and then failed with 'no operator-facing answer after bounded recovery', and a model that still wanted a tool could never get one. The plain no-tools stream() raised on a tool call complete() recovers and streamed raw DSML before quarantine, and dsml.py only knew the '<｜DSML｜ calls>' spelling. Providers now raise ProviderToolCallError for malformed calls and tool-refusal frames and flag the stream error tool_call_rejected; chat treats that as a tool_call attempt, keeps answer text beside a call, cuts the answer at the first unreadable DSML tag, routes once more when synthesis asks only for a tool the turn can still afford, completes with the answer written before a rejected call when recovery is spent, and names reasoning-only exhaustion. dsml.py reads function_calls/tool_calls frames, string= attributes and JSON invoke bodies, and finds any DSML tag anywhere. The new file test_chat_final_synthesis_recovery.py drives the loop through the real OpenRouter adapter and scripted providers; the selected test_chat/test_providers/test_dsml/test_chat_tool_loop/test_chat_api node ids are the new, edited and directly affected tests.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: the real-Core journeys never make a provider emit a malformed or refused tool call during synthesis; the Python tests drive those paths directly. Whole test_chat.py, test_providers.py, test_chat_tool_loop.py and the other chat suites were run locally (all green) and are not selected per the CI-scoping rule. No full suites.
